Dyno Nobel Returns to Annual Profit, Forecasts Earnings Lift
By Rhiannon Hoyle
​Dyno Nobel returned to profit in fiscal year 2026 and said it expects a further increase in earnings from its explosives business in the year ahead.

The Australia-based company said it made a net profit of 66.1 million Australian dollars (US$45.4 million) in the 12 months ended Sept. 30 versus a loss of A$53.2 million a year ago. Analysts expected a profit of A$176.5 million, according to a consensus estimate collated by Visible Alpha.
Directors declared a final dividend of 5.0 Australian cents a share, down from 9.5 Australian cents a year ago and in line with consensus estimates.

Underlying earnings before interest and taxes in its explosives business, excluding material items, totaled A$485.1 million. That was up from A$433.6 million the year prior and in line with guidance for underlying Ebit between A$480 million and A$490 million.
The company said it expects underlying Ebit of between A$515 million and A$555 million in fiscal 2027.
